connection.address_hint: A host name or IP address, with :port when it is not 7300; or a full http(s):// address. Pasting the URL the engine printed (with ?token=…) fills the token too.
connection.failure_title: The remote engine cannot be used
connection.foot_local: Switching restarts the app on this computer's engine and workspace.
connection.foot_remote: Saving tests the engine first, then restarts the app on it.
connection.lead: Where the engine runs: this computer, or another computer of yours that runs npm run serve (for example over Tailscale). This window then shows that engine's runs, projects and settings.
connection.local_help: The default: the app runs the engine and its workspace here.
connection.now_remote: This window shows the engine on {host}.
connection.quit_title: Quit the app (this is its only window)
connection.remote_help: Only the window runs here; runs, terminals and files are on the engine's computer.
connection.title: Engine connection
connection.token_hint: The engine's MULTIAGENT_SERVER_TOKEN. Kept encrypted in this computer's app data, never in the workspace.
dialog.in_use_detail:
It is open in {who}. Two copies on one workspace would take each other's runs for interrupted and start them twice.

Open a scratch copy (your agents, skills, workflows and settings copied to a new workspace; simulations only), or quit.
dialog.in_use_message: This workspace is already open in another copy of the app
dialog.workspace_detail: It holds the run logs and cloned repositories. The path is saved and reloaded the next time the app opens.
dialog.workspace_gone:
The registered workspace folder no longer exists:
{path}
nav.arena.title: Up to five models write the same document, critique each other, and the best parts are merged
nav.discovery.title: Shape accepted ideas until they are ready: Triage, Shape, Define, Ready
nav.duo.title: Layout preview: writer and reviewer agents in a chat
nav.inbox.title: Capture raw ideas privately and triage them
nav.nightwatch.title: Night watch: what the Oracle may do while you are away, and how each night went
nav.projects.title: Your projects: each one's runs, conflict map, architecture and refactors
nav.releases.title: What shipped and what the next release holds: checked by the release workflow, pushed only on your Ship
nav.roadmap.title: Ordered stages of runs: each stage starts when the previous one has finished and merged
nav.sessions.title: Claude Code, Codex and Grok sessions on this machine, in embedded terminals
notify.chain_body: Open the run to see its chain.
notify.conflict_body: The local base conflicts with origin.
notify.fallback_body: {agent} fell back in {step}: {from} → {to} ({reason}). The provider may be out of credits.
notify.findings_body: The Oracle is paused, so it cannot look at what Self-healing detected. {text}
notify.interrupted_body: The app closed while the run was in progress. Resume it from the run screen.
notify.live_body: Open the Roadmap to see it.
notify.live_budget: Live roadmap stopped: daily budget reached
notify.live_empty: Live roadmap: nothing left to pick
notify.live_failed: Live roadmap paused: the refill failed
notify.memory_body: {step} ran `{command}` again and the memory guard stopped it again ({used} GB, over the {limit} GB limit).
notify.merged_locally: Merged locally into {base}, not pushed yet.
notify.night_body: Open the Night watch to see the night.
notify.oracle_body: Open the Oracle to see what it did.
notify.po_body: Open the Backlog to read the answer.
notify.po_failed: The Product Owner could not answer: {project}
notify.session_body: The CLI stopped and is waiting for your answer.
notify.stray_body: PID {pid}, {share}% of a core: {command}. Stop it with memory:stopStray, or end it in the Task Manager.
notify.stray_title: A process of a finished run keeps using CPU: {run}
settings.agents.intro: Agent sessions are opened with these CLIs. A CLI that is not signed in shows its sign-in command; Run setup again walks through installing and signing in to each one.
settings.app_update.checking: Checking whether this app runs from a project of this workspace…
settings.app_update.help: After a roadmap stage ends, the app updates itself from the local main of the project that is its repository: it pauses the roadmap, waits for the runs in progress (a gate is never answered), fast-forwards, restarts and resumes the roadmap. It never pushes.
settings.app_update.title: Apply merged fixes to this app
settings.app_update.up_to_date: the app is up to date
settings.backlog.group_help: The most issues Assign workflow sends as one run (one branch, one PR/MR that closes all of them).
settings.backlog.platform_help: Where the Backlog screen syncs a project's issues from. It can be changed on the Backlog screen too. GitHub uses the gh CLI and GitLab the glab CLI; Bitbucket sync is not available yet.
settings.backlog.refresh_help: The Backlog offers to run Backlog Refresh (it updates the issues' paths, lines and done tasks) when the last refresh is older than this and the base branch got merges since. It never starts a run by itself.
settings.backlog.title: Backlog
settings.backlog.workflow_help: Used wherever a workflow is not picked by hand: the Product Owner's plans, Split + roadmap, Create + roadmap, the Assign dialog with nothing remembered. Unset: the local workflow (no push, no PR, no CI) when the workspace has it.
settings.backlog.workflow_missing: {missing} no longer exists: {file} is used instead.
settings.base.on_red_help: After a merge, the full unit suite runs on the base in a clean worktree, in simulation (#405). A test red there, or counted as pre-existing by 2 runs, files a bug issue; with a fix item, a new stage at the front of the roadmap fixes it. Nothing is pushed and no gate is answered.
settings.base.title: Base check
settings.budget.day_help: Per calendar day, every roadmap, the live roadmap's refills and the Night watch included. Empty: no cap.
settings.budget.intro: What real runs spend (live runs included; Codex runs priced from tokens × the model prices of Usage). When the next roadmap item's estimate would pass a budget, the roadmap pauses before starting it and tells you: raise it for today, or resume anyway. A run already started finishes; no gate is answered. The top bar shows today's spending against it.
settings.budget.night_help: While the Night watch is on, from its start. Empty: no cap (the daily one still applies).
settings.budget.title: Budget
settings.concurrency.max_help: A new run is refused while this many are in progress (when several workflows are allowed). A value you set is kept, on any machine.
settings.concurrency.per_project_help: So one project's queue can't take every slot. Empty: no limit per project.
settings.concurrency.several: Allow several workflows at the same time
settings.concurrency.several_help: Off: one run at a time. On: runs start while there are free slots, and the Backlog queues fill them. Each run works in its own git worktree.
settings.concurrency.sims_help: Off: simulated runs (no CLI, no cost) start even when the real runs use every slot.
settings.concurrency.title: Concurrent runs
settings.concurrency.workers_help: Each run's agents and suite get it as MULTIAGENT_TEST_WORKERS and pass it to the test runner (--workers, --maxWorkers, -n).
settings.control.unavailable: Not available in the browser client
settings.deps.help: Each project's dependencies are installed once per lockfile and linked into the runs' worktrees. Entries no worktree uses are removed after 14 days or above 20 GB; clearing keeps the ones in use.
settings.deps.kept: ; {count} kept: in use by a worktree or an install
settings.deps.label: Dependencies
settings.deps.nothing: Nothing cached yet: the first run of a project installs once.
settings.deps.title: Dependency cache
settings.engine.browser_help: This page is served by the engine on {host}. The desktop app on another computer can show this engine too: Settings › Execution › Engine there.
settings.engine.local_help: This computer runs the engine: runs, terminals and the workspace are here. Another computer of yours can run it instead (npm run serve), and this app becomes its window.
settings.engine.remote_help: This window shows the engine on {host}: runs, terminals, files and settings are on that computer. Change… switches back to this computer or to another engine (the app restarts).
settings.engine.title: Engine
settings.execution.chip_help: Shows the share of the last 24 h with at least one run active (green from 90%, amber from 60%, red below). A click opens Analytics › 24/7.
settings.execution.confirm_stop_help: Ask for confirmation when clicking Stop.
settings.execution.control: Allow outside sessions to control this app
settings.execution.control_help: A terminal or another agent on this computer can read runs, the backlog and settings and act on roadmaps through a local endpoint (control/endpoint.json) with the multiagent-ctl client. Human gates stay closed to it.
settings.execution.developer_help: Shows the "Simulation" checkboxes, checked by default, and the simulation scenarios of Write & Review. Simulated runs call no CLI and cost nothing. Off: every run is real.
settings.execution.keep_awake_help: Keeps this computer from sleeping while runs or a roadmap are active (this workspace; also on the Workflows screen). The display may still turn off; choosing Sleep, closing the lid and the Windows power plan still apply.
settings.execution.notify_oracle: Notify when the Oracle acts under Night watch
settings.execution.notify_oracle_help: A desktop notification for each repair the Oracle makes without asking while its Night watch is on.
settings.execution.notify_po: Notify when the Product Owner answers
settings.execution.notify_po_help: A desktop notification when the Backlog's Product Owner answers a question. Not shown while this window shows its drawer for that project.
settings.execution.notify_runs_help: A desktop notification when a run starts, waits for you at a gate, succeeds, fails, is cancelled or was interrupted. Not shown while this window is focused on that run.
settings.execution.notify_sessions: Notify when a session waits for you
settings.execution.notify_sessions_help: A desktop notification when a CLI in a Sessions terminal stops and waits for your answer (a question, a permission prompt, the end of its turn). Not shown while this window is focused on that terminal.
settings.execution.open_run_help: Switch to the sessions screen as soon as a workflow starts.
settings.execution.retention_help: Days the notification center (the bell at the top right) keeps notifications; older ones are deleted. 0: keep them all.
settings.fallbacks.intro: When an agent's provider runs out of credits or hits its usage limit, its turn moves on to the next entry, in order (provider:model, e.g. codex:gpt-6-luna), for the rest of the run. Used for an agent whose workflow declares no fallbacks.
settings.fallbacks.label: Fallbacks of {provider}
settings.fallbacks.row: Out of credits on {provider}: try these next.
settings.fallbacks.saved: Saved: the next runs use them.
settings.fallbacks.title: Fallbacks
settings.findings.button_help: For the people building this app: freeze the view, mark what is wrong and save it with the state behind it, or file it as an issue (Ctrl+Shift+F). Always shown when the app runs from source.
settings.findings.empty: No findings yet: the Findings button saves them here.
settings.findings.saved_help: In the workspace's findings/ folder, newest first.
settings.findings.title: Findings
settings.folders.skills: Skills (one folder with a SKILL.md per skill).
settings.folders.title: Folders
settings.general.registry_help: The workspace path is loaded from here the next time the app opens.
settings.general.workspace_help: Where runs, repos, projects, skills and settings.json live.
settings.healing.help: The Oracle watches every run and roadmap, day and night, and repairs what its permissions allow. It never answers a gate, pushes, closes an issue or deletes data.
settings.healing.perms_title: Opens the Night watch's checklist: one list for both
settings.healing.title: Self-healing
settings.healing.unavailable: The Oracle cannot start in this workspace, so Self-healing cannot be turned on.
settings.healing.unavailable_short: The Oracle cannot start in this workspace
settings.index.help: A SQLite index next to the files: the runs list cache, the Backlog queues, the gates waiting for you and the notifications. The files stay the source of truth: rebuilding reads every run again from runs/.
settings.index.title: Index
settings.index.unavailable: Not available: {error}. Everything still works from the files.
settings.language.agents_help: Chat replies, the prose of step outputs, handoff notes, decision logs and documents. Same as the interface: the Interface language above. JSON keys, paths, branches and code comments stay as they are.
settings.language.interface_help: The language of the app's screens, menus and notifications. Until one is chosen: this computer's language when the app has it, else English.
settings.language.issues_help: Issues, issue comments, PR/MR descriptions and commit messages: what goes to the repository. Checkboxes, #n references, labels and closing keywords (Closes #n) stay as they are.
settings.language.title: Language
settings.limits.intro: An agent on this model gets its turn timeout multiplied by the factor; a run with an agent on it may spend up to the cost limit (when it is above the workflow's). A workflow's own models win.
settings.limits.invalid: A factor or a cost limit is a positive number.
settings.limits.title: Limits per model
settings.live.budget_help: The live roadmap's runs and refills over the last 24 hours; once reached, it ends after its current stages and adds nothing more. 0: no cap.
settings.live.budget_label: Live roadmap daily budget in USD
settings.live.cap_help: A refill picks open issues with a complexity:n label up to this value, lowest first; issues without one are left out.
settings.live.refresh_help: Sync the backlog from its platform before the Product Owner reads it, so it picks from current issues.
settings.live.refresh_label: Sync the backlog before a refill
settings.live.stages_help: The most stages the Product Owner adds each time the roadmap's last stage ends.
settings.live.title: Live roadmap
settings.machine.auto_hint: The values below follow this machine.
settings.machine.evidence: Days: {days}. Runs held or stopped: {runs}. Nothing changes until you apply it.
settings.machine.manual_hint: Your values: {runs} at once, {workers} per run; they stay as they are on any machine.
settings.machine.suggestion: The memory guard stepped in on {days} days this week: lower to {runs}?
settings.machine.unknown_hint: Today's defaults apply; type values below to set your own.
settings.machine.unread: This machine's threads and memory couldn't be read.
settings.memory.floor: Hold while free memory is under (%)
settings.memory.floor_help: Suites and new runs wait while less than this share of the memory is free (a suite at most 10 minutes). 0: never hold. Between 0 and 50.
settings.memory.limit: Stop a process over (% of the RAM)
settings.memory.limit_hint: Between 5 and 90. Measured as committed memory on Windows, resident memory elsewhere.
settings.memory.limit_label: Memory limit per process, percent of the RAM
settings.memory.stop_help: A test, a build or a script a real run started that passes the limit below is stopped with its children, before it exhausts the machine. The agent CLI itself, the app and your other programs are never stopped.
settings.memory.title: Memory guard
settings.oracle.budget_help: Once today's Oracle spend reaches it, questions are refused until tomorrow (UTC); an answer already running is not cut. It also counts in the monthly Claude Code budget. 0: no cap.
settings.oracle.compact_help: When a turn's context passes this size, the next question starts a new session from the skill, the memory and a handoff note. The history is kept.
settings.oracle.park: Move on past a gate after (minutes)
settings.oracle.park_help: With the Night watch's "Skip an item" permission, a roadmap run waiting this long at a human gate, with nothing else of its roadmap running, is moved past: the next stage starts and the gate keeps waiting for you.
settings.oracle.park_label: Minutes at a gate before the Night watch moves on
settings.oracle.title: Oracle
settings.oracle.wake_help: Which runs' events wake the Oracle: every run (except the runs you mute from its chat), only the runs and roadmaps it watches, or none. Each wake-up is one short model call, batched over 30 seconds.
settings.oracle.wake_on_help: Routine events (agent output, tool calls, steps starting) never wake it.
settings.phone.address_help: Your private https address for the page (Tailscale or Cloudflare Tunnel), used in the gate links. Empty: the links use this computer's address.
settings.phone.intro: Answer the human gates from your phone: a page with only the open gates, for your paired phones. An agent, a script or the supervisor never answers through it.
settings.phone.pair_help: A one-time code, valid 10 minutes. Turns the page on.
settings.phone.port_help: The page's port on this computer (127.0.0.1). The next free port is used when it is taken.
settings.phone.qr_alt: QR code to pair a phone
settings.phone.reachable_help: Whether the page answers on this computer and at the address from outside.
settings.phone.revoke_body: Its gates page stops working at once; pair it again to use it.
settings.phone.step_address: Paste that https address in Address from outside above, Save, and press Check: the gate links in the notifications use it.
settings.phone.step_link: A gate link works for that gate only, for 30 minutes; every answer asks you to confirm, showing what the button does.
settings.phone.step_listen: The page listens on {url}, on this computer only. It shows only the open gates: nothing else of the app is served there.
settings.phone.step_pair: Press Pair a phone and scan the QR code with the phone (or open the page and type the code). The phone keeps its own token: revoke it here at any time.
settings.phone.step_reach: To reach it from your phone, privately: install Tailscale on this computer and on the phone (same account) and run tailscale serve --bg {port}; only your devices reach the https address it prints. Or a named Cloudflare Tunnel to {url} behind a Cloudflare Access policy that allows only your email. Never a public address without access rules.
settings.time_zone.help: Times on every screen, where days, nights and months start (Analytics, Usage, budgets, the Oracle's daily limit) and the times the agents report. Until one is chosen: this computer's.
settings.time_zone.label: Time zone
settings.title: Settings
settings.voice.intro: Dictate into any field with the OS: Win+H on Windows, Dictation on macOS (press Fn twice). Or use the mic button on the long text fields (or Ctrl+Shift+M): the recording is transcribed on this machine by whisper.cpp, inserted at the cursor for review, and deleted right after. Nothing leaves the machine.
settings.voice.language_help: The language you speak. Auto detects it on each recording (less reliable on short ones).
settings.voice.model_help: Bigger models transcribe better and slower. Downloaded once into the app's data folder.
settings.voice.not_downloaded: Not downloaded yet. It goes to {dir}.
settings.voice.title: Voice input
setup.agents.lead: Each agent turn runs one of these CLIs on this computer: install the ones you want and sign in to them.
setup.agents.name: Agents
setup.agents.title: Connect your agents
setup.all_ready: Every bundled workflow can run on this computer.
setup.check_again_help: After installing or signing in, press Check again (or end its terminal: the rows check again by themselves).
setup.come_back: You can go on and come back later from Settings › Agents & CLIs.
setup.optional_forge: Optional: Backlog sync and pull requests
setup.project.empty_help: Add the folder of a repository you work on. Simulations do not need one.
setup.project.finish_help: Finish opens Start on your first picked workflow.
setup.project.lead: A project is the folder or repository the workflows work on.
setup.project.name: First project
setup.project.title: Add your first project
setup.skip_body: Nothing more is changed. You can run it again from Settings › Agents & CLIs.
setup.try.lead: See a whole workflow run before it spends anything.
setup.try.name: Try it safely
setup.try.real: Real runs use your own CLI subscriptions or API credits: each agent turn is billed by its provider.
setup.try.runs_help: Sized from this machine's threads and memory. Turn on several runs at once, or set your own values, in Settings › Execution › Concurrent runs.
setup.try.show_help: Adds a Simulation checkbox to Start, checked by default. Turn it off later in Settings › Execution › Developer mode.
setup.try.simulation: A simulation runs the whole flow (steps, gates, results) with made-up answers: no CLI is called and nothing is spent.
setup.without_core: Without {names}, no workflow runs for real (simulations still do).
setup.workflows.lead: The picked workflows are offered in Start; the others stay in Workflows › Definitions.
setup.workflows.name: Workflows
setup.workflows.none: No bundled workflows found in the workspace's workflows/ folder.
setup.workflows.none_picked: None picked: Start keeps offering them all.
setup.workflows.picked_help: Workflows › Definitions › Show in Start changes it later; nothing is deleted.
setup.workflows.ready_title: Everything it needs is installed and signed in
setup.workflows.title: Pick your workflows
shell.sign_in_lead: Create a free account. It only tells us how many people use the app.
shell.sign_in_waiting: Finish signing in in your browser…
shell.sim_only_title: MULTIAGENT_SIMULATION_ONLY is set: real runs and CLI terminals are refused, only simulations run.
